summary: Fingerprint reader becomes unresponsive after Windows 11 22H2 in-place upgrade during provisioning
description:
Issue summary:
During our automated provisioning task sequence (SCCM-based) that performs an in-place upgrade from Windows 10 to Windows 11 22H2, the integrated fingerprint readers on several device SKUs stop responding post-upgrade. Devices finish the TS successfully, users can log in with password, but biometric login and Windows Hello setup fail and the fingerprint device does not appear in Device Manager or appears with an exclamation mark.

Impact:
- ~180 corporate devices in the last 48 hours (primarily Dell/Lenovo/HP fleet) unable to use fingerprint login.
- Blocks onboarding flow for some new hires; increases support overhead for re-provisioning or manual driver reinstalls.

Environment:
- Provisioning flow: SCCM task sequence that runs Win10->Win11 22H2 in-place upgrade image, then installs OEM driver bundle from package driver-bundle-v5.
- Affected region: us-west production provisioning pool.

Observed behavior:
- Windows Hello fingerprint setup throws: "No fingerprint devices are available".
- Windows Biometric Service (WbioSrvc) fails to start consistently.
- Device Manager shows biometric device either absent or as "Unknown device" with code 45/28.

Expected behavior:
- Biometric device present post-upgrade and OEM drivers loaded; Windows Hello setup available.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Pick affected Dell Latitude 7540 with Windows 10 21H2 baseline image.
2) Run SCCM task sequence that performs in-place upgrade to Windows 11 22H2 and applies driver-bundle-v5 and company-provisioning.ps1.
3) Complete TS and OOBE for corporate user.
4) Attempt to setup Windows Hello -> Fingerprint.

Repro rate:
- Intermittent but ~40% on same SKU in the last run. Less frequent on HP fleet (~10%).

Relevant logs and artifacts included below.
steps_to_reproduce:
1. Execute SCCM TS: TSID 2026-PR-012 (Win10->Win11 22H2 in-place).
2. Ensure driver-bundle-v5 is applied (current package in distribution point).
3. After first user login perform: > sc query WbioSrvc and check Device Manager.
4. Capture: msinfo32 export, pnputil /enum-devices, Get-WindowsUpdateLog, and provisioning logs at C:\Windows\ccm\Logs\smsts.log.
logs:
Sample event excerpts:

Application: Windows Biometric Service (WbioSrvc)
Timestamp: 2026-03-10 02:14:37
Message: Service failed to start. Error 0x80070005

System Event ID 1536:
Device USB\VID_138A&PID_00XX not migrated due to partial or mismatched driver stack. Status: 0xC0000185

smsts.log snippet:
[2026-03-10 02:04:21] Downloading package: driver-bundle-v5
[2026-03-10 02:06:03] Driver install returned code 0x80190001 (driver package signature mismatch)
investigation_notes:
Initial triage (Aisha): Confirmed correlation with driver-bundle-v5 application stage.
Hypotheses:
- The OEM driver bundle includes legacy Win10-signed drivers incompatible with 22H2 driver-signing changes.
- SCCM applies drivers before the new kernel driver store hooks are initialized, causing PnP migration failures.
- Windows Biometric Service configuration gets corrupted and fails to start due to missing provider DLLs.

Reproduction tests (Marcus):
- Re-ran TS with driver-bundle-v4 (older) -> biometric works on 2/3 Dell units but fails on one.
- Manually reinstalling OEM driver INF via pnputil /add-driver ... /install temporarily shows device then WbioSrvc still fails to start with Access Denied when service startup attempted.
- Checked signature via Get-AuthenticodeSignature on OEM driver INF: shows SHA1 and SHA256 signatures but timestamping inconsistent between vendor certs.

Next steps planned:
- Create a trimmed driver package with only the biometric driver and signed cert chained to Microsoft (test package: driver-bio-trim-2026-03-11).
- Run TS with the trimmed package and add a 30s pause after upgrade to allow kernel post-upgrade hooks.
- Engage OEM support with vendor-signed driver artifacts and request a Microsoft-signed driver or guidance.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Aisha Patel: Pushed initial alert to #internal-support. Attached smsts.log and two msinfo32 exports from affected devices.

2026-03-10 11:45 - Marcus Lee: Reproduced locally on Dell Latitude 7540. Driver installation returned signature mismatch for one of the infs. Attempted pnputil staging — device enumerates but WbioSrvc reports ACCESS_DENIED on StartService.
2026-03-11 08:03 - IT Field Ops (Carla N.): Reported two users at 03/10 new-hire orientation had to skip fingerprint enrollment; ended up enrolling PIN only. Will provide serials and imaging job IDs.
2026-03-11 14:22 - Marcus Lee: Uploaded test package driver-bio-trim-2026-03-11 and queued TS run on 5 canary devices. Monitoring results expected by EOD 2026-03-12.

2026-03-12 10:01 - Marcus Lee: Canary run results: 4/5 devices now show biometric device and Windows Hello setup succeeds after trimmed package. One device still fails; investigating hardware revision edge-case. Proceeding to plan staged rollout for remaining devices tomorrow with rollback steps documented.

2026-03-12 15:40 - Aisha Patel: Notified Support and Solutions Engineering to prepare KB for helpdesk steps (manual temporary workaround: provide enrollment via USB external fingerprint dongle if urgent).
resolution:
Workaround and remediation plan in progress. Actions taken so far:
- Created trimmed biometric-only driver package 'driver-bio-trim-2026-03-11' which restored biometric functionality on 80% of canary devices.
- For devices that still fail: manual re-stage via pnputil + restart of WbioSrvc, followed by user-driven Windows Hello enrollment, works in many cases.
- Plan: staged deployment via SCCM over next 48 hours in 3 waves (Canary: 20 devices; Wave1: 60 devices; Wave2: remainder ~100 devices). Rollback: rerun TS with driver-bundle-v3 if regressions found.
- OEM engagement: opened case with vendor (Case ID: OEM-2026-334) requesting a Microsoft-signed driver and confirmation of compatibility with 22H2.
- Post-deploy checklist created: verify Device Manager enumeration, sc query WbioSrvc == RUNNING, and successful Windows Hello enrollment.

Follow-ups:
- Solutions Eng to create a short KB article for field support with pnputil and service restart commands.
- Hardware team to audit failing serials for unusual firmware revisions.
- Re-evaluate current driver-bundle packaging process to prefer vendor-signed drivers chained to Microsoft.
